# Psalm 75 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choir director: to the tune of 'Do Not Destroy.' A psalm of Asaph. A song. We thank you, God — oh, we thank you! Your name is near, and people can't stop talking about your amazing works.

**2** God says: 'When the right moment comes, I will judge fairly.

**3** When the earth and everyone on it is shaking, I'm the one holding the pillars steady.' Selah

**4** 'I tell the proud: Stop your bragging! I tell the wicked: Don't flex your power.

**5** Don't raise your fist toward heaven or speak with arrogant defiance.'

**6** Promotion doesn't come from the east or the west, and it doesn't come from the wilderness.

**7** It's God alone who judges — he brings one person down and raises another up.

**8** The LORD holds a cup of foaming, spiced wine in his hand; he pours it out, and every wicked person on earth will drink it down to the last drop.

**9** But I will keep declaring this forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.

**10** I will shatter the power of the wicked, but the strength of the righteous will be raised high.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **75:2-3**: God's voice breaking into the psalm is electrifying. While the world is falling apart, God calmly says: 'I'm the one holding the pillars.' That's reassurance at a cosmic level.

- **75:8**: The cup of God's judgment is one of the Bible's most vivid images — foaming, spiced wine that the wicked must drink to the dregs. It shows up again in Revelation 14.

— PNEUMA
